# DRL-021: Build canonical evidence-first Wix workshop pages

## Metadata

- Milestone: M4
- Labels: `wix`, `design`
- Owning mission: 6
- Evidence owner: Brand/Web
- Requirement IDs: `DRL-WEB-001`, `DRL-WEB-006`
- Dependencies: DRL-003
- Director decisions: RES-013, RES-014, RES-015
- Status: QUEUED — the repository documentation contract is ready; Wix editor
  implementation and visual acceptance evidence remain outstanding.
- Public contract impact: COMPATIBLE — existing broad routes redirect into the
  five-page tree; no working public artifact URL is removed.

## User / research value

Give an academic evaluator or research-oriented employer fast, honest evidence
of the Director's research questions and systems ability. The canonical journey
is workshop thesis -> recorded run -> `TR-2026-001` -> methods/limitations ->
projects, source, and contact.

## Problem

The live Wix site and older foundation documents use a broad institutional
hierarchy, collaborator-first journeys, and service-shaped Atticus language.
That presentation obscures the strongest current evidence: signed success and
degraded replays, `TR-2026-001`, and an honestly inconclusive Stage-B model
bake-off.

## Scope

### In scope

- Implement Home, Projects, Writing, Open Source, and About.
- Lead with **Watch a recorded run** and **Read TR-2026-001**.
- Make the degraded replay and Stage-B no-winner result visible.
- Present Atticus as a documented research artifact and its subdomain as planned.
- Keep contributor routes secondary and teaching under Writing/Methods.
- Preserve first-person, one-person workshop language.
- Update redirects, metadata, evidence links, mobile layouts, and fallbacks.
- Update tests, docs, screenshots, and WORKLOG handoff together.

### Out of scope

- Deploying a public Atticus service or changing its trust boundary.
- Creating a fictional collaboration program, staff, department, or institute.
- Publishing employer names or confidential/proprietary work.
- Unrelated refactors, dependency upgrades, or cloud deployment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Five-page map and redirects are implemented and exported.
- [ ] The first actions are **Watch a recorded run** and **Read TR-2026-001**.
- [ ] Success and degraded replay links work, disclose prototype/demo-signature
      limits, and have static fallbacks.
- [ ] `TR-2026-001` has a full reading surface with methods, limitations,
      citation, source, and correction history.
- [ ] The Stage-B no-winner board and all six blocking reasons are visible.
- [ ] Atticus is labeled as a research artifact; no launch action implies a live
      service before deployment evidence exists.
- [ ] Project maturity and verification dates come from controlled metadata.
- [ ] Phone/tablet/laptop, keyboard, screen reader, contrast, zoom, reduced
      motion, broken embed, and unavailable-service states are reviewed.
- [ ] Footer links work; fabricated uptime and institutional chrome are absent.
- [ ] No secrets, employer data, silent analytics, or overstated live claims.
- [ ] Required checks and mission verification matrix pass with exact results.

## Verification plan

```bash
make docs-check
uv run pytest -q tests/docs/test_brand_consistency.py tests/docs/test_website_positioning.py tests/test_domain_wix.py
make verify
```

The Wix operator also records link checks, responsive captures, keyboard and
screen-reader notes, and the saved revision used for rollback.

## Security / privacy / licensing / cost

This issue changes no application authority. Wix and browser code contain no
credentials or private-backend tokens. Public analytics require consent and
minimal collection. Replays use public/synthetic fixture data and disclose demo
signing. Open-source, open-weight, and source-available labels follow actual
artifact terms. No new cloud cost is authorized.

## Rollback

Restore the saved Wix revision and preserve the previous redirect map. Revert the
repository change if controlled copy or contract validation regresses.

## Evidence required for closure

Commands and exact results, Wix revision, page/redirect export, desktop/mobile
captures, replay/report/fallback links, accessibility notes, link results,
custom-code/data inventory, commit/PR, and updated handoff.
